text:
University College London (UCL) was founded on February 11, 1826, as London University, an alternative to the Anglican universities of Oxford and Cambridge. Initially operating as a joint stock company, its first warden was Leonard Horner, the first scientist to lead a British university. Although philosopher Jeremy Bentham is considered its "spiritual father," his direct involvement was limited.
UCL was incorporated by royal charter as University College, London, on November 28, 1836. It gained a supplemental charter in 1878, making it the first British university to grant degrees to women, admitting them to Arts, Law, and Science faculties that same year. UCL merged into the University of London in 1907 and formally changed its name to University of London, University College. The college achieved its own taught and research degree-awarding powers in 2005. UCL is a founding member of the Russell Group and the League of European Research Universities.
